conditions.description: iam:PassedToService conditions on the PassRole grant may restrict passing roles to Amplify.

Code must run under the new role, through a build with a changed buildSpec/environment (service role) or a deployed SSR runtime the source controls (compute role); automatic builds or webhooks can replace StartJob.

aws-amplify-updateapp-passrole.mitigation: Restrict iam:PassRole on Amplify roles with iam:PassedToService=amplify.amazonaws.com and specific role ARNs; restrict amplify:UpdateApp.
aws-amplify-updateapp-passrole.notes: The source needs at least one existing app it can update (amplify:UpdateApp on that app). Both iamServiceRoleArn and computeRoleArn require iam:PassRole on the target role.
aws-amplify-updateapp-passrole.summary: The source can obtain the privileges of passable roles trusting amplify.amazonaws.com by assigning them as an app's service (build) or compute role and running code under them.

target.aggregate_as: Roles trusting amplify.amazonaws.com passable in {account}

aws-amplify-updateapp-passrole.title: Repoint an Amplify app's service or compute role to a passed role and build it

conditions.description: The app must have an IAM service role configured (trusting amplify.amazonaws.com); otherwise builds run without AWS permissions.

aws-amplify-updateapp-startjob.mitigation: Restrict amplify:UpdateApp/UpdateBranch and StartJob; keep Amplify service roles least-privileged.
aws-amplify-updateapp-startjob.notes: StartJob Resource is the branch ARN (app ARN prefix); the evaluator should treat app-ARN wildcards as covering branches. amplify:UpdateBranch can be an equivalent build-spec change path. Severity critical when the attached role is admin-equivalent.
aws-amplify-updateapp-startjob.summary: The source can obtain the privileges of the IAM service role attached to an Amplify app whose build it can reconfigure and run.

target.aggregate_as: Service roles of Amplify apps covered by amplify:UpdateApp in {account}

aws-amplify-updateapp-startjob.title: Change an Amplify app build specification and start a build

conditions.description: The app must have an IAM service role configured (trusting amplify.amazonaws.com); otherwise builds run without AWS permissions.

The existing build must start an interpreter that loads a startup environment variable pointing at content reachable in the build workspace; a branch buildSpec override was observed not to be executed.
Automatic builds or an incoming webhook can replace amplify:StartJob as the trigger.

aws-amplify-updatebranch-startjob.mitigation: Restrict amplify:UpdateBranch, amplify:UpdateApp and amplify:StartJob to deployment administrators and keep Amplify service roles least-privileged.
aws-amplify-updatebranch-startjob.notes: Branch ARNs are under the app ARN; the evaluator should treat app-ARN wildcards as covering branches and jobs. No iam:PassRole is needed when the existing service role is reused. Severity critical when the attached role is admin-equivalent.
aws-amplify-updatebranch-startjob.summary: The source can obtain the privileges of the IAM service role of an Amplify app whose branch build environment it can change and build.

target.aggregate_as: Service roles of Amplify apps with branches covered by amplify:UpdateBranch in {account}

aws-amplify-updatebranch-startjob.title: Change an Amplify branch's build environment variables and start a build

conditions.description: An AWS-service integration calls one configured service action per integration; the source can create several, but reachable actions are those exposed by AWS integrations, so effective privilege is close to but not always fully the role's.
The integration must be invoked, which needs a deployment (POST) or apigateway test invocation; resource policies or authorizers on existing APIs do not apply to new APIs the source creates.

aws-apigateway-integration-credentials-p.mitigation: Restrict iam:PassRole for apigateway.amazonaws.com roles and apigateway write actions to API administrators.
aws-apigateway-integration-credentials-p.notes: HackTricks demonstrates the Lambda AWS_PROXY integration, where the credentials role is only used to invoke the chosen function and does not hand the caller the function's execution role; reach beyond that relies on an AWS-service integration URI calling other service actions with the same credentials role, hence conditional and medium severity. Existing integrations already holding a role are reachable with PATCH+POST without PassRole (role attached to an integration); the evaluator may model that as attached_resource_covered_by apigateway:PATCH.
aws-apigateway-integration-credentials-p.summary: The source can obtain the privileges of passable roles trusting apigateway.amazonaws.com by using them as the execution credentials of an AWS-service integration it can invoke.

target.aggregate_as: Roles trusting apigateway.amazonaws.com in {account}

aws-apigateway-integration-credentials-p.title: Create a REST API AWS-service integration that runs with a passed credentials role

conditions.description: AppConfig uses the retrieval role only to fetch the configured source; the source obtains that source's content, not a role session or arbitrary API calls.
The secret, parameter, document or object ARN and a deployable version must be known, and an existing application, environment and deployment strategy must be in scope of the AppConfig actions.
The retrieval role also needs kms:Decrypt on the source's customer-managed key when one is used.
iam:PassedToService conditions may restrict which roles can be passed.

aws-appconfig-passrole-createconfigurati.mitigation: Restrict iam:PassRole on AppConfig retrieval roles with iam:PassedToService and exact role ARNs, scope each retrieval role to its own configuration sources, and limit external-source configuration profile creation to AppConfig administrators.
aws-appconfig-passrole-createconfigurati.notes: Bounded impact - delegated data read of what the retrieval role can read, not a role session (same modelling as the DataSync bounded PassRole entries). Replaces the exclusion of this heading.
aws-appconfig-passrole-createconfigurati.summary: The source can exercise the read privileges of a passable role trusting appconfig.amazonaws.com over Secrets Manager secrets, Parameter Store parameters, SSM documents or S3 objects by making it the retrieval role of an external-source configuration profile it deploys and reads.

target.aggregate_as: Roles trusting appconfig.amazonaws.com passable in {account}

aws-appconfig-passrole-createconfigurati.title: Read another service's data through a passed AppConfig retrieval role

conditions.description: AppFlow uses the role only for the Glue table, database and partition operations of the flow's catalog registration; no credentials and no arbitrary actions under the role.
Referenced connector profiles also need appflow:UseConnectorProfile, and an S3-destination flow needs the caller-side S3 bucket permissions.
iam:PassedToService conditions may restrict which roles can be passed.

aws-appflow-passrole-glue-catalog.mitigation: Restrict iam:PassRole on AppFlow catalog roles with iam:PassedToService and exact role ARNs, scope those roles to dedicated Glue databases, and limit flow creation and update.
aws-appflow-passrole-glue-catalog.notes: Bounded impact - catalog-integrity proxy through the passed role (page states it is privilege escalation but not role credential theft). Modelled like the DataSync bounded PassRole entries.
aws-appflow-passrole-glue-catalog.summary: The source can exercise the Glue Data Catalog table and partition create/update privileges of a passable role trusting appflow.amazonaws.com by setting it as the metadata-catalog role of a flow it creates or updates and runs.

target.aggregate_as: Roles trusting appflow.amazonaws.com passable in {account}

aws-appflow-passrole-glue-catalog.title: Use a passed AppFlow role to create or update Glue Data Catalog tables

conditions.description: The fleet must be running and associated with a stack; CreateStreamingURL authorizes the stack ARN (the edge is computed only for grants covering "*").

The streamed application or desktop must let the user run code or reach the instance's role credential profile; locked-down application-only stacks with restricted file system and clipboard settings may prevent it.
Fleets using Elastic or application-mode streaming need an application the user is allowed to launch.

aws-appstream-createstreamingurl-existin.mitigation: Restrict appstream:CreateStreamingURL to the identity broker, attach least-privilege roles to fleets and prefer SAML or user-pool access with entitlements over API-minted streaming URLs.
aws-appstream-createstreamingurl-existin.notes: Fleet instances expose the fleet IamRoleArn through the appstream_machine_role credential profile. Fleet-to-stack association is not collected, so every role trusting appstream.amazonaws.com is reported with unknown attachment.
aws-appstream-createstreamingurl-existin.summary: The source can obtain the privileges of the IAM role of existing AppStream fleets associated with a stack it can create streaming URLs for.

target.aggregate_as: IAM roles of AppStream fleets in {account}

aws-appstream-createstreamingurl-existin.title: Open a streaming session on an existing fleet that has an IAM role

conditions.description: A user (or the source, through a streaming URL) must launch the application on a fleet that has an IAM role.
The new launch path or parameters must run content the source controls (for example from an app block it can write).

aws-appstream-updateapplication-elastic-.mitigation: Restrict appstream:UpdateApplication and app block sources to packaging administrators and attach least-privilege roles to Elastic fleets.
aws-appstream-updateapplication-elastic-.notes: {target.consumer_input_arn} is the AppStream application ARN; the application-to-fleet mapping is not collected.
aws-appstream-updateapplication-elastic-.summary: The source can obtain (when a user next launches the application) the privileges of the IAM role of fleets that run an application it can update.

target.aggregate_as: IAM roles of AppStream fleets running updatable applications in {account}

aws-appstream-updateapplication-elastic-.title: Change the launch definition of an application used by an Elastic fleet

conditions.description: The source must provide an image it controls, or an S3 session-script ZIP readable by AppStream in the fleet account and Region.
The fleet must launch an instance or user session so the controlled image or session script runs.

aws-appstream-updatefleet-image-swap.mitigation: Restrict appstream:UpdateFleet on fleets with IAM roles, validate images and session-script S3 objects, and monitor changes to fleet image and session-script settings.
aws-appstream-updatefleet-image-swap.notes: The same UpdateFleet permission and fleet-role target cover both image substitution and an Elastic fleet session-script location change. The session-script variant is documented at aws-persistence/aws-appstream-persistence/README.md#appstreamupdatefleet--s3--recurring-system-session-scripts-on-an-existing-elastic-fleet. A role swap instead requires iam:PassRole.
aws-appstream-updatefleet-image-swap.summary: The source can obtain the IAM role privileges of an existing fleet by supplying a controlled image or session-script archive that runs on later fleet instances.

target.aggregate_as: IAM roles of AppStream fleets in {account}

aws-appstream-updatefleet-image-swap.title: Replace an existing AppStream fleet image or session-script archive while retaining its role

conditions.description: A live Spark 3.5 session must exist in the workgroup and its ID be known to the source.

aws-athena-getsessionendpoint-spark-conn.mitigation: Restrict athena:GetSessionEndpoint to session owners and keep Spark execution roles least-privileged.
aws-athena-getsessionendpoint-spark-conn.notes: The returned bearer token controls the existing session; no PassRole is needed.
aws-athena-getsessionendpoint-spark-conn.summary: The source can obtain the privileges of the execution role of Spark workgroups whose active Spark Connect sessions it can attach to.

target.aggregate_as: Execution roles of Athena Spark workgroups in {account}

aws-athena-getsessionendpoint-spark-conn.title: Obtain the Spark Connect endpoint and token of an active Athena Spark session

conditions.description: batch:SubmitJob must cover both the job definition and a job queue (Resource includes both ARNs).

aws-batch-submitjob-existing-definition.mitigation: Scope batch:SubmitJob to specific job definitions and queues; keep job roles least-privileged.
aws-batch-submitjob-existing-definition.notes: Registering a new job definition with a passed role is covered by aws-batch-registerjobdefinition-passrole-submitjob. Compute-environment instance roles may also be reachable from EC2-backed jobs. The baked jobRoleArn is an ECS task role (trusts ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com), so the selector resolves through the ECS task principal rather than batch.amazonaws.com; job definitions are not collected, so the attachment is unknown. EKS-backed jobs use a Kubernetes service account and are not covered.
aws-batch-submitjob-existing-definition.summary: The source can obtain the privileges of the job role of an existing job definition by submitting a job with a container command override.

target.aggregate_as: Job roles of Batch job definitions covered by batch:SubmitJob in {account}

aws-batch-submitjob-existing-definition.title: Submit a job using an existing job definition with a job role

conditions.description: iam:PassedToService conditions may restrict which roles can be passed.
Harness creation also needs CreateWorkloadIdentity, GetAgentRuntime and related read actions; CreateMemory may be needed depending on configuration.
The account must already have the AWSServiceRoleForBedrockAgentCoreRuntimeIdentity service-linked role, or the source must be able to create it.

aws-bedrock-agentcore-createharness-pass.mitigation: Scope iam:PassRole to dedicated low-privilege AgentCore roles with iam:PassedToService=bedrock-agentcore.amazonaws.com and deny bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand unless direct shell access is required.
aws-bedrock-agentcore-createharness-pass.notes: Composite operation; only the core actions are modelled and the remaining provisioning actions are a condition.
aws-bedrock-agentcore-createharness-pass.summary: The source can obtain the privileges of any passable role trusting bedrock-agentcore.amazonaws.com by creating a harness with that execution role and running commands in its runtime.

target.aggregate_as: Roles trusting bedrock-agentcore.amazonaws.com passable in {account}

aws-bedrock-agentcore-createharness-pass.title: Create an AgentCore harness with a passed execution role and run shell commands in it

conditions.description: The runtime must have a ready endpoint the source can address; runtimes are not collected, so any role trusting bedrock-agentcore.amazonaws.com is a candidate.

aws-bedrock-agentcore-invokeagentruntime.mitigation: Deny bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand except where direct shell access is required, and keep runtime execution roles least-privileged.
aws-bedrock-agentcore-invokeagentruntime.notes: The harness heading shows InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand giving a shell as the runtime's execution role; on an existing runtime neither iam:PassRole nor any create action is needed.
aws-bedrock-agentcore-invokeagentruntime.summary: The source can obtain the privileges of the execution role of an existing AgentCore agent runtime (including harness runtimes) by running commands in it.

target.aggregate_as: Execution roles of AgentCore runtimes covered by bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand in {account}

aws-bedrock-agentcore-invokeagentruntime.title: Run shell commands in an existing AgentCore agent runtime

conditions.description: Only APPLY_IAM_POLICY (managed policy to users/groups/roles), APPLY_SCP_POLICY (management account) and RUN_SSM_DOCUMENTS (stop EC2/RDS documents) are possible; the gain is what the role can do through these, not a full role session.
The action runs only when the budget threshold is crossed (automatic approval) or after budgets:ExecuteBudgetAction approval; an existing budget the source can attach the action to is required.
iam:PassedToService conditions may restrict which roles can be passed.

aws-budgets-passrole-createbudgetaction.mitigation: Restrict iam:PassRole on budget execution roles and budgets:CreateBudgetAction to finance administrators; scope execution roles to the policies and targets intended.
aws-budgets-passrole-createbudgetaction.notes: With APPLY_IAM_POLICY and a role allowed to attach any managed policy, the source can attach AdministratorAccess to itself.
aws-budgets-passrole-createbudgetaction.summary: The source can make a passable role trusting budgets.amazonaws.com attach IAM policies or SCPs, or run SSM documents, on its behalf (bounded by the three budget action types).

target.aggregate_as: Roles trusting budgets.amazonaws.com passable in {account}

aws-budgets-passrole-createbudgetaction.title: Create a budget action that runs as a passed execution role

conditions.description: The role is used only for the configured source, processors and sinks; no credentials are returned and impact is bounded by the pipeline elements and runtime source/sink validation.
Starting a pipeline needs a supported Kinesis Video source and valid sink resources.
iam:PassedToService conditions may restrict which roles can be passed.

aws-chime-passrole-mediainsightspipeline.mitigation: Restrict iam:PassRole on media-pipelines roles with iam:PassedToService=mediapipelines.chime.amazonaws.com and exact role ARNs, and scope those roles to their own streams and sinks.
aws-chime-passrole-mediainsightspipeline.notes: Bounded impact - privilege proxy over media and sink resources the role can access, not a role session (DataSync bounded PassRole precedent).
aws-chime-passrole-mediainsightspipeline.summary: The source can exercise the media read and sink privileges (Kinesis Video, Lambda, Kinesis Data Streams, S3, SQS, SNS) of a passable role trusting mediapipelines.chime.amazonaws.com by storing it in a media insights pipeline configuration and starting a pipeline.

target.aggregate_as: Roles trusting mediapipelines.chime.amazonaws.com passable in {account}

aws-chime-passrole-mediainsightspipeline.title: Use a passed media-pipelines role through a media insights pipeline configuration

conditions.description: A later stack update must resolve the parameter again (supplied parameter kept with its previous key); the source does not control the trigger.
Impact depends on the property consuming the value (policy ARNs, trust principals, AMI IDs, code locations, endpoints); a value used only for non-sensitive settings yields no privilege.
SecureString parameters with a customer-managed key need kms:Encrypt on that key for the overwrite.

aws-cloudformation-ssm-parameter-poisoni.mitigation: Restrict ssm:PutParameter on deployment-consumed parameter namespaces, pin security-sensitive values to reviewed versions or ordinary template parameters, and alert when a parameter write precedes a stack operation that resolves it.
aws-cloudformation-ssm-parameter-poisoni.notes: {target.consumer_input_arn} is the Parameter Store parameter ARN named by the stack's SSM parameter-typed template parameter; that mapping is not collected, so the edge is unknown until it is. Same modelling as aws-cloudformation-nested-template-s3-poisoning. Unversioned dynamic references are not guaranteed to refresh and are not covered.
aws-cloudformation-ssm-parameter-poisoni.summary: The source can obtain (on a later legitimate stack update) the privileges of a stack's stored service role when a security-sensitive property of that stack is taken from an SSM parameter-typed template parameter whose Parameter Store value the source can overwrite.

target.aggregate_as: Service roles of stacks resolving writable Parameter Store values in {account}

aws-cloudformation-ssm-parameter-poisoni.title: Overwrite a Parameter Store value that a stack resolves as a template parameter

conditions.description: The first Lambda@Edge association in an account also needs iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole.
The function must be created in us-east-1.

aws-cloudfront-lambda-edge-passrole.mitigation: Restrict iam:PassRole on Lambda@Edge roles and cloudfront:UpdateDistribution.
aws-cloudfront-lambda-edge-passrole.notes: trust_allows_service given as a list means every listed principal must be trusted. Roles trusting only lambda.amazonaws.com are reachable through the generic Lambda PassRole technique (lambda.yaml) instead. The Lambda@Edge permissions page writes the replication permission as lambda:EnableReplication*; the concrete action in the Service Authorization Reference is lambda:EnableReplication.
aws-cloudfront-lambda-edge-passrole.summary: The source can obtain the privileges of passable roles trusting both lambda.amazonaws.com and edgelambda.amazonaws.com by running a Lambda@Edge function it controls on a distribution it can update.

target.aggregate_as: Roles trusting lambda and edgelambda in {account}

aws-cloudfront-lambda-edge-passrole.title: Associate a new Lambda@Edge function with a passed role to a distribution

conditions.description: An execution must start afterwards (EventBridge source-change rule, schedule, operator or source-held StartPipelineExecution).
A downstream action must execute content from the pushed revision (buildspec, template, deploy scripts).
codecommit:References conditions or approval-rule templates may block direct pushes to the source branch.
GitPush does not include GitPull; the source needs an existing working copy or enough history to build a valid update.

aws-codecommit-gitpush-pipeline-source.mitigation: Restrict codecommit:GitPush on pipeline source branches with codecommit:References conditions, require reviewed pull requests, separate source publishers from pipeline runners and add approval gates before privileged stages.
aws-codecommit-gitpush-pipeline-source.notes: {target.consumer_input_arn} is the CodeCommit repository ARN configured as a pipeline source. attached_to_service codepipeline means roles of the executing downstream actions, not the pipeline role. Direct CodeBuild sources are covered by aws-codecommit-gitpush-codebuild-source.
aws-codecommit-gitpush-pipeline-source.summary: The source can obtain (at the next execution) the privileges of the roles of downstream pipeline actions (CodeBuild projects, CloudFormation deploy roles) that build or deploy content from a CodeCommit branch it can push to.

target.aggregate_as: Roles of downstream actions of pipelines with writable CodeCommit sources in {account}

aws-codecommit-gitpush-pipeline-source.title: Push to a CodeCommit repository branch used as a pipeline source

conditions.description: The instance uses SAML identity management and the source can assume the federation role with an arbitrary RoleSessionName matching the victim's case-sensitive Connect username.
The federation role's connect:GetFederationToken grant is not restricted to the intended per-user identity pattern.

aws-connect-saml-session-name-impersonat.mitigation: Prevent arbitrary RoleSessionName selection on Connect federation roles (sts:RoleSessionName conditions) and restrict connect:GetFederationToken to the caller's own user.
aws-connect-saml-session-name-impersonat.notes: Contact-center administration only; the Connect token is not AWS credentials. The requirement is evaluated on the source; when the source reaches it only through the federation role, that role's edge carries the chain.
aws-connect-saml-session-name-impersonat.summary: The source can obtain the Amazon Connect application privileges (for example the Admin security profile) of any SAML Connect user whose username it can use as its role-session name.

target.aggregate_as: Amazon Connect administrators in {account}

aws-connect-saml-session-name-impersonat.title: Impersonate a SAML Connect user by choosing the role-session name

conditions.description: The source must already control an EC2 instance; Disassociate is only needed when the instance already has a profile.

aws-ec2-passrole-associate-instance-prof.mitigation: Restrict instance-profile association actions and iam:PassRole on EC2 roles.
aws-ec2-passrole-associate-instance-prof.summary: The source can obtain the privileges of passable roles trusting ec2.amazonaws.com in existing instance profiles by attaching such a profile to an instance it controls.

target.aggregate_as: Roles trusting ec2.amazonaws.com with an instance profile in {account}

aws-ec2-passrole-associate-instance-prof.title: Associate or replace the instance profile of an instance the source controls

aws-ecr-putimagetagmutability.mitigation: Restrict ecr:PutImageTagMutability and reference images by digest.
aws-ecr-putimagetagmutability.notes: Distinct from aws-ecr-push-consumed-tag only for immutable repositories.

aws-ecr-setrepositorypolicy.notes: Same-account principals named in a repository policy get access without an identity-policy grant, except ecr:GetAuthorizationToken which is registry-level.
aws-ecr-setrepositorypolicy.summary: The source can obtain the privileges of roles of workloads running images from a repository whose policy it can rewrite to grant itself push access.

target.aggregate_as: Roles of workloads running images from repositories covered by ecr:SetRepositoryPolicy in {account}

aws-ecr-setrepositorypolicy.title: Rewrite a private repository policy to grant the source push access

Disabling session tags on the association can bypass trust conditions that expect eks-cluster-* tags only when those conditions use *IfExists or Null checks.

aws-eks-updatepodidentityassociation-pas.mitigation: Restrict eks:UpdatePodIdentityAssociation as tightly as eks:CreatePodIdentityAssociation and scope iam:PassRole to the intended roles.
aws-eks-updatepodidentityassociation-pas.notes: Useful when CreatePodIdentityAssociation is denied but updates are allowed.
aws-eks-updatepodidentityassociation-pas.summary: The source can obtain the privileges of any passable role trusting pods.eks.amazonaws.com by swapping it into an existing Pod Identity association whose pods it can run or control.

aws-eks-updatepodidentityassociation-pas.title: Repoint an existing EKS Pod Identity association to another passable role

Depending on the environment's deployment policy, additional Auto Scaling/EC2/ELB permissions may be required.

aws-elasticbeanstalk-createapplicationve.mitigation: Restrict elasticbeanstalk:CreateApplicationVersion and UpdateEnvironment to the deployment pipeline on specific applications and environments.
aws-elasticbeanstalk-createapplicationve.notes: Reach is the instance profile of the environments covered by UpdateEnvironment.
aws-elasticbeanstalk-createapplicationve.summary: The source can obtain the privileges of the EC2 instance-profile role of existing environments it can deploy a new version to.

target.aggregate_as: Instance-profile roles of updatable Beanstalk environments in {account}

aws-elasticbeanstalk-createapplicationve.title: Deploy an attacker-hosted application version to an existing environment

EventBridge validates the universal-target action at creation and blocks some services and actions; reach is the role's permissions on supported actions only, and results are not returned.
iam:PassedToService conditions may restrict which roles can be passed.

aws-events-passrole-createsubscriber-uni.mitigation: Restrict events:CreateSubscriber to bus owners, scope iam:PassRole on EventBridge roles with iam:PassedToService=events.amazonaws.com, and keep delivery roles least-privileged.

A subscriber on a cross-account shared bus runs as a role of the subscriber owner's account.
aws-events-passrole-createsubscriber-uni.summary: The source can obtain the write privileges of any passable role trusting events.amazonaws.com, exercised through the supported service actions of a universal target.

target.aggregate_as: Roles trusting events.amazonaws.com passable in {account}

aws-events-passrole-createsubscriber-uni.title: Create an enhanced-bus subscriber with a universal target and a passed role

The cluster code location must be readable by the service.
iam:PassedToService conditions may restrict which roles can be passed.

aws-finspace-passrole-createkxcluster.mitigation: Restrict iam:PassRole on FinSpace execution roles and finspace:CreateKxCluster, and keep execution roles least-privileged.
aws-finspace-passrole-createkxcluster.notes: Documentation-grounded; Managed kdb environments are rare. CreateKxUser/UpdateKxUser role binding is not modelled.
aws-finspace-passrole-createkxcluster.summary: The source can obtain the privileges of passable roles trusting finspace.amazonaws.com by running q code it supplies in a kdb cluster under that role.

target.aggregate_as: Roles trusting finspace.amazonaws.com passable in {account}

aws-finspace-passrole-createkxcluster.title: Create a FinSpace Managed kdb cluster with a passed execution role

conditions.description: A stream session started with a RoleArn must be live; the role is only exposed for the session lifetime.

The action authorizes the parent stream-group ARN; the "*" requirement matches any CreateStreamSessionAdminShell grant by overlap, so the specific stream group holding the role-bearing session must be within the grant.

aws-gameliftstreams-createstreamsessiona.mitigation: Restrict gameliftstreams:CreateStreamSessionAdminShell to operators and give session roles only what the application needs.
aws-gameliftstreams-createstreamsessiona.notes: Stream sessions are not collected; attachment resolves as unknown. No iam:PassRole is needed because the backend already attached the role.
aws-gameliftstreams-createstreamsessiona.summary: The source can obtain the privileges of the role of live GameLift Streams sessions in stream groups it can open admin shells in.

target.aggregate_as: Roles of live GameLift Streams sessions in {account}

aws-gameliftstreams-createstreamsessiona.title: Open an admin shell in a live stream session that has a role

conditions.description: Only escalates if a non-default version of a covered policy grants more (ideally admin) permissions than the current default; the evaluator should compare stored policy versions.

aws-iam-setdefaultpolicyversion-self.mitigation: Delete obsolete permissive policy versions and restrict iam:SetDefaultPolicyVersion to administrators.
aws-iam-setdefaultpolicyversion-self.notes: Severity becomes critical when a stored non-default version is admin-equivalent.
aws-iam-setdefaultpolicyversion-self.summary: The source can obtain the privileges of a more permissive stored version of a policy attached to itself.

aws-iam-setdefaultpolicyversion-self.title: Switch the default version of a customer-managed policy attached to the source

conditions.description: iam:UpdateGroup is authorized on both the current and the new group ARN, and iam:AddUserToGroup must cover the group at its new path; the evaluator only checks that some group path is covered.

aws-iam-updategroup-path-move.mitigation: Treat iam:UpdateGroup as a membership-management permission and avoid path-scoped iam:AddUserToGroup grants.

For service-account-backed compilation results or workflow configs strict act-as mode requires caller actAs on the effective SA; that path is covered by gcp-dataform-workflow-invocation-actas.

gcp-dataform-workflowconfig-end-user-inv.mitigation: Prefer dedicated service accounts over end-user credentials for Dataform workflows, restrict dataform.workflowInvocations.create on such repositories, and deny end_user_auth_config with a custom organization policy constraint.
gcp-dataform-workflowconfig-end-user-inv.notes: Replaces gcp-dataform-scheduled-workflow-code-tamper; at 171e422 HackTricks no longer treats internal-repository commit poisoning as a current path, because strict act-as mode blocks cron releases for repositories without a third-party remote. Google's docs do not explicitly state which caller permission triggers a user-credential config, so this follows HackTricks.
gcp-dataform-workflowconfig-end-user-inv.summary: The source can make the saved actions of a user-credential Dataform workflow configuration run as the Google Account that authorized it, without iam.serviceAccounts.actAs.

target.aggregate_as: Google Accounts whose stored Dataform user credentials back workflow configs the source can invoke

gcp-dataform-workflowconfig-end-user-inv.title: Trigger an existing Dataform workflow configuration that runs with a Google Account's user credentials

conditions.description: HackTricks states scheduled pipeline runs in the pinned namespace execute as that SA; on RBAC-enabled instances the namespace SA is the design-time identity, so whether runtime code (compute profile) also uses it depends on the instance version and profile configuration.
A code-capable plugin (PySpark Program, Scala Spark) must be installed, and the Data Fusion service agent must be able to act as / mint tokens for the chosen SA.
The caller also needs effective datafusion.instances.get on the instance.

gcp-datafusion-namespace-setserviceaccou.mitigation: Grant actAs only on dedicated Data Fusion namespace SAs and restrict datafusion.namespaces.setServiceAccount to platform administrators.
gcp-datafusion-namespace-setserviceaccou.notes: The recurring schedule is persistence and is not modelled; the edge is the namespace SA pin plus pipeline execution.
gcp-datafusion-namespace-setserviceaccou.summary: The source can obtain the privileges of any service account in the project on which it holds iam.serviceAccounts.actAs, by setting it as a Data Fusion namespace service account and deploying and running pipelines in that namespace.

target.aggregate_as: Service accounts pinnable as Data Fusion namespace SA in {project}

gcp-datafusion-namespace-setserviceaccou.title: Pin a Data Fusion namespace to a chosen service account and run pipelines as it

conditions.description: A code-capable plugin (PySpark Program, Scala Spark) must be installed; uploading one needs datafusion.artifacts.create/update.
The Data Fusion service agent must already be able to act as the profile's SA; no caller actAs is needed.
Pipeline permissions may be granted per namespace on RBAC-enabled instances.

gcp-datafusion-pipelines-create-execute.mitigation: Restrict roles/datafusion.developer and higher; use a low-privilege pipeline SA per compute profile instead of the Compute Engine default SA.
gcp-datafusion-pipelines-create-execute.summary: The source can obtain the privileges of the pipeline VM service account of Data Fusion instances where it can create and execute pipelines (PySpark / Scala Spark plugins run arbitrary code on the Dataproc cluster).

target.aggregate_as: Pipeline VM SAs of Data Fusion instances where the source can run pipelines

gcp-datafusion-pipelines-create-execute.title: Deploy and run a code-capable Data Fusion pipeline as the pipeline VM service account

conditions.description: The source must also route bus events into the pipeline, with eventarc.enrollments.create plus eventarc.messageBuses.use on the bus, or eventarc.enrollments.update on an existing enrollment (create/use are not in the permission catalog, so this is kept as a condition).

The pipeline project's Eventarc service agent needs iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken on the SA (roles/eventarc.serviceAgent supplies it for same-project SAs; cross-project SAs need an explicit grant).
At least one matching event must traverse the enrollment (a legitimate event, or one injected with eventarc.messageBuses.publish); enrollment, pipeline and bus must share a region.

The attacker HTTPS endpoint must be reachable from Eventarc (internal endpoints need a network attachment); Google's guidance to use OAuth only for *.googleapis.com is not an enforced host restriction.

gcp-eventarc-pipeline-oauth-token-actas.mitigation: Grant actAs only on dedicated Eventarc SAs, restrict eventarc.pipelines.create and enrollments, and alert on pipelines with non-googleapis.com OAuth destinations.
gcp-eventarc-pipeline-oauth-token-actas.notes: The token scope defaults to cloud-platform. roles/eventarc.developer lacks actAs and messageBuses.use. Standard-trigger OIDC tokens are audience-bound and not modelled.
gcp-eventarc-pipeline-oauth-token-actas.summary: The source can obtain an access token, and so the privileges, of any service account on which it holds iam.serviceAccounts.actAs, by routing bus events through a pipeline whose HTTPS destination it controls.

target.aggregate_as: Service accounts usable as Eventarc pipeline OAuth identity in {project}

gcp-eventarc-pipeline-oauth-token-actas.title: Create an Eventarc Advanced pipeline that sends a service account's OAuth token to an attacker endpoint

conditions.description: Entitlements with "Activate access without approvals" activate at the requested time; otherwise the required number of other approvers must approve, because PAM does not allow approving your own request.

Only the entitlement's roles, IAM conditions and maximum duration are granted (legacy Owner/Editor/Viewer are not supported); escalation to scope owner needs an IAM-management role, otherwise the impact is that role's permissions for the grant duration.
PAM must be onboarded at the scope and its service agent must keep authority to add and remove the temporary binding.

gcp-pam-entitlement-request-grant.mitigation: Require approval on entitlements offering IAM-management roles, keep requester lists small and avoid broad groups as requesters.
gcp-pam-entitlement-request-grant.notes: Google states requesters and approvers need no PAM-specific permissions and that you cannot approve your own request. Entitlement creation needs the scope's setIamPolicy, so it is not modelled as an escalation. Outcome role_activation (time-bound activation of an eligible role, like Entra PIM) replaces the default scope_control because full scope control holds only when the offered role manages IAM. The evaluator still returns None for gcp_pam_entitlement_requester, so the edge is not emitted until the collector reads entitlements.
gcp-pam-entitlement-request-grant.summary: A principal listed as a requester of a Privileged Access Manager entitlement can temporarily obtain the entitlement's roles on its project, folder or organization; when those roles manage IAM, it gains IAM control of that scope.

target.aggregate_as: IAM control of {target.scope} through a PAM entitlement

gcp-pam-entitlement-request-grant.title: Request a temporary IAM-admin grant through a PAM entitlement the source is eligible for

conditions.description: A consumer must explicitly preview, deploy or update the poisoned version in their project; nothing runs at update time.
The product must already be attached to a catalog associated with the consumer hierarchy, and the modified asset must pass validation.
Terraform-based solutions run as the configured or default Cloud Build identity instead of the cloudservices agent.

gcp-privatecatalog-product-version-poiso.mitigation: Restrict cloudprivatecatalogproducer editor/admin roles and review solution versions before consumers deploy them.
gcp-privatecatalog-product-version-poiso.notes: Deployment Manager solutions run as the consumer project's Google APIs Service Agent (roles/editor by default), like gcp-deploymentmanager-deployments-create.
gcp-privatecatalog-product-version-poiso.summary: The source can make the Google APIs Service Agent of consumer projects that later deploy a shared solution version it can update create attacker-chosen resources.

target.aggregate_as: Google APIs Service Agents of projects deploying poisoned Service Catalog solutions

gcp-privatecatalog-product-version-poiso.title: Replace the template of a shared Service Catalog solution version that consumers deploy

conditions.description: Emit only a conditional/MANUAL edge when the exact source, resource, and target join; missing or unsupported facts are UNKNOWN, never a derived/FAIL path. Add cross-directory source principal and exact sync rule join; new effective group membership is conditional on next successful sync, and only existing IAM-bound Google group is target.

gcp-v3-17-join-a-gcp-iam-bound-workspace.mitigation: Restrict the named capability and verify the exact execution, credential or trust relationship.
gcp-v3-17-join-a-gcp-iam-bound-workspace.notes: Collector request recorded in privesc-v3-collector-requests.md. Absent or incomplete evidence is UNKNOWN/unresolved; verified evidence remains conditional.
gcp-v3-17-join-a-gcp-iam-bound-workspace.summary: External directory group-member write + configured Directory Sync mapping -> IAM-bound Google group membership. Exact source, target, scope and prerequisite proof are required.

target.aggregate_as: Exact targets for Join a GCP IAM-bound Workspace group by changing its synchronized external-directory group

gcp-v3-17-join-a-gcp-iam-bound-workspace.title: Join a GCP IAM-bound Workspace group by changing its synchronized external-directory group

conditions.description: Emit only a conditional/MANUAL edge when the exact source, resource, and target join; missing or unsupported facts are UNKNOWN, never a derived/FAIL path. F14: simulate one authorized update and required certificateTemplates.use/issuance. Other remaining restrictions must still pass.

gcp-v3-42-relax-issuance-constraints.mitigation: Restrict the named capability and verify the exact execution, credential or trust relationship.
gcp-v3-42-relax-issuance-constraints.notes: Collector request recorded in privesc-v3-collector-requests.md. Absent or incomplete evidence is UNKNOWN/unresolved; verified evidence remains conditional.
gcp-v3-42-relax-issuance-constraints.summary: Pool/template update relaxes exact issuance restriction, then #40 trust chain. Exact source, target, scope and prerequisite proof are required.

target.aggregate_as: Exact targets for Relax issuance constraints

gcp-v3-42-relax-issuance-constraints.title: Relax issuance constraints

conditions.description: The restored provider must already accept an identity the source controls and a matching IAM binding must remain.
Deleted pools/providers are restorable for approximately 30 days.

gcp-wif-pool-provider-restore.mitigation: Remove IAM bindings of decommissioned pools before deleting them and restrict pool/provider update and undelete.
gcp-wif-pool-provider-restore.notes: Also covers pools.update (re-enable) and pools.undelete. Provider re-enable through workloadIdentityPoolProviders.update is modelled by gcp-wif-provider-update. Disabling a provider blocks only new exchanges; disabling a pool also blocks use of issued tokens.
gcp-wif-pool-provider-restore.summary: The source can obtain the privileges of service accounts and roles still bound to principals of disabled or deleted workload identity pools or providers it can restore.

target.aggregate_as: SAs and roles bound to principals of restorable WIF pools

gcp-wif-pool-provider-restore.title: Re-enable or undelete a pool or provider that still trusts attacker-controlled credentials

conditions.description: Only effective when the pool has a binding for all its identities (principalSet .../workloadIdentityPools/<pool>/*) or for attribute values the new provider can assert.
The pool must be enabled.

gcp-wif-provider-create.mitigation: Restrict workloadIdentityPoolProviders.* (roles/iam.workloadIdentityPoolAdmin), avoid pool-wide bindings and restrict allowed providers by org policy.
gcp-wif-provider-create.summary: The source can obtain the privileges of service accounts and roles bound to pool-wide principals of workload identity pools on which it holds workloadIdentityPoolProviders.create.

target.aggregate_as: SAs and roles bound to pool-wide principals of controllable WIF pools

gcp-wif-provider-create.title: Add a provider trusting attacker-controlled credentials to a pool with broad bindings

conditions.description: An IAM binding must exist for a subject, group or mapped attribute the modified provider can assert, and the provider's attribute condition must be satisfiable.
The provider and pool must be enabled.

gcp-wif-provider-update.mitigation: Restrict workloadIdentityPoolProviders.update and alert on provider metadata/issuer changes.
gcp-wif-provider-update.notes: SAML metadata updates must keep one current certificate, which does not prevent adding another. An OIDC oidc.jwksJson upload replaces discovery-fetched keys while keeping the issuer URI.
gcp-wif-provider-update.summary: The source can obtain the privileges of service accounts and roles bound to principals of workload identity pools whose providers it can update.

target.aggregate_as: SAs and roles bound to principals of WIF pools with updatable providers

gcp-wif-provider-update.title: Change an existing provider's trust configuration

conditions.description: An existing IAM binding must cover a workforce principal, group, attribute or pool-wide set that the created, changed or restored provider can assert; no target policy is changed.
Pool/provider restore only helps while attacker-usable trust and a matching binding remain, within the recovery window.
A locally uploaded OIDC JWKS works only for programmatic STS exchange, not federated console sign-in.

gcp-wif-workforce-provider-control.mitigation: Restrict workforce pool/provider administration (roles/iam.workforcePoolAdmin, roles/iam.workforcePoolEditor) at the organization and avoid pool-wide bindings.
gcp-wif-workforce-provider-control.notes: Workforce pools are organization-scoped and their principals usually receive roles directly; those direct grants need the proposed gcp_federated_principal kind. Only service accounts that grant token creation or workloadIdentityUser to workforce principals are reachable today.
gcp-wif-workforce-provider-control.summary: The source can obtain the privileges of service accounts that grant impersonation to principals of workforce pools whose providers or state it controls.

target.aggregate_as: SAs and roles bound to principals of controllable workforce pools

gcp-wif-workforce-provider-control.title: Create, change or restore a workforce pool provider to admit an attacker-controlled external user

conditions.description: If the config sets service-account scopes, users also need actAs on the SA at launch/use time.
Using another developer's workstation also exposes that user's session data; IAM on workstations is granted per workstation or config.

gcp-workstations-use-existing-workstatio.mitigation: Grant roles/workstations.user per workstation only to its owner and restrict workstations.*.setIamPolicy (roles/workstations.policyAdmin, roles/workstations.admin, roles/owner).
gcp-workstations-use-existing-workstatio.notes: Connection tokens from generateAccessToken cannot be revoked and last up to 24h.
gcp-workstations-use-existing-workstatio.summary: The source can obtain the privileges of the service accounts of existing workstations it can use or whose IAM policy it controls.

target.aggregate_as: SAs of Cloud Workstations the source can connect to

gcp-workstations-use-existing-workstatio.title: Connect to an existing workstation (directly or after an IAM self-grant) and use its SA

conditions.description: EKS needs an IMDS hop limit >= 2 (AL2023 managed node groups without a launch template and Auto Mode default to 1) and no disablePodIMDS; GKE needs node pools without Workload Identity/metadata concealment; AKS needs no network policy blocking 169.254.169.254.
An egress NetworkPolicy denying the metadata address removes the edge.

k8s-cloud-pod-imds-node-identity.mitigation: Block pod access to IMDS (hop limit 1, disablePodIMDS, GKE Workload Identity, egress policies) and use workload identities instead.
k8s-cloud-pod-imds-node-identity.notes: Admission is not involved; only network reachability matters. Exec into existing pods gives the same reach and is modelled implicitly through the ServiceAccount chain.
k8s-cloud-pod-imds-node-identity.summary: The source can obtain the privileges of the node cloud identity by creating any pod when pods can reach the instance metadata service.

target.aggregate_as: Cloud identity of nodes in {cluster}

k8s-cloud-pod-imds-node-identity.title: Ordinary pod reaches the node metadata service

conditions.description: With --default-service-account the HelmRelease impersonates a tenant ServiceAccount; controller arguments are not collected.
The default Flux install binds cluster-admin to helm-controller.

k8s-workloads-flux-helmrelease-controlle.mitigation: Enable Flux multi-tenancy lockdown and restrict HelmRelease and Flux source creation.
k8s-workloads-flux-helmrelease-controlle.notes: Chart values, hooks and dependencies all render under the controller identity (see helm-template-injection.md).
k8s-workloads-flux-helmrelease-controlle.summary: The source can obtain the privileges of the Flux helm-controller ServiceAccount by creating a HelmRelease (and a chart source it controls) that the controller installs with its own identity.

target.aggregate_as: Flux helm-controller of {cluster}

k8s-workloads-flux-helmrelease-controlle.title: Create a Flux HelmRelease without a ServiceAccount so helm-controller installs it

conditions.description: The controller flag --default-service-account (Flux multi-tenancy lockdown) makes Kustomizations without spec.serviceAccountName impersonate a tenant ServiceAccount instead; controller arguments are not collected.
The default Flux install binds cluster-admin to kustomize-controller (cluster-reconciler ClusterRoleBinding); the reached privileges are those of that binding.
The source object must point to content the principal controls; source-controller network egress and --no-cross-namespace-refs may restrict it.

k8s-workloads-flux-kustomization-control.mitigation: Enable Flux multi-tenancy lockdown (--default-service-account, --no-cross-namespace-refs) and restrict who can create Kustomizations and Flux sources.
k8s-workloads-flux-kustomization-control.notes: Selected by ServiceAccount name in any namespace (usually flux-system). Patching an existing Kustomization's path/sourceRef is modelled by k8s-workloads-flux-kustomization-patch-controller-identity.
k8s-workloads-flux-kustomization-control.summary: The source can obtain the privileges of the Flux kustomize-controller ServiceAccount by creating a Kustomization (and a source it controls) that the controller reconciles with its own identity.

target.aggregate_as: Flux kustomize-controller of {cluster}

k8s-workloads-flux-kustomization-control.title: Create a Flux Kustomization without a ServiceAccount so kustomize-controller applies it
